title: The 19-service target does not say whether the sandbox is one database per service or one shared sandbox, or where the generator's build module lives
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 and 13 (one sandbox database rwb_sandbox, one pipeline stage, package recovery.tools.sandbox); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 9, 15, 29 and 41 (one ACE PostgreSQL server, 19 rwb_* schemas, one login each, no sandbox); Template and Rules v1 R5.5 DP-01, DP-02 and DP-15
section: 3 Preconditions; 4 Flow; 12.7 Tables owned; 13 Solution plan; 17 Guardrails
description: The legacy story gives one sandbox database for the whole monolith, one pipeline stage and one generator package, and it says nothing about how many sandboxes the 19-service target needs or where the generator artifact sits. Architecture v5 gives one ACE PostgreSQL server with 19 service schemas and one login each, and no sandbox database at all, so neither the count of sandbox databases nor the packaging boundary of the build tool can be read from the source set.
evidence: Legacy section 3 'A PostgreSQL 17 database rwb_sandbox exists in DEV'; legacy section 13 'folder tools/sandbox-generator, Java package recovery.tools.sandbox, built as a separate build module that is not packaged into the ACE service'; Architecture v5 slide 29 '19 RECOVERY SCHEMAS - ONE LOGIN EACH' with no sandbox row; slide 41 service catalogue with no sandbox entry
proposed: Read the target as one DEV sandbox database per service release: rwb_sandbox for rwb-source-data with the build database rwb_sandbox_next, built by tools/sandbox-generator in package th.co.scb.ace.workbench.recovery.sourcedata.sandbox as a separate build module that the service artefact does not contain. A shared sandbox would breach DP-01 and DP-02 because one login per service cannot hold objects of three schemas owned by two teams. Confirm the count at the wave 1 entry check and record it in the Environment and Deployment Design.

title: The contract of a build tool is described by no source, so the story has to read it as the pipeline stage interface
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 section 12 (Pipeline stage table: trigger, job name, schedule, input, output, events published, idempotency key, restart behavior); section 13 build steps; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 (12.1 to 12.9) and R5.5 DP-15
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 11 Data; 12 Contract; 13 Solution plan
description: No source in the set describes a contract for a pipeline stage or a build tool: the architecture gives contracts for REST, events, Temporal, files and SQL views only, and the legacy story describes its stage inside the story body and the solution plan. The six contract criteria of this story therefore have no source text to copy, and their shape is a reading, not a quotation.
evidence: Architecture v5 slide 11 'Five call types, each with a fixed contract' (REST, Event, Temporal, File, SQL view) with no build-tool row; legacy section 12 'Pipeline stage' table and section 13 'Build steps'; Template and Rules v1 R7.2 s12 which lists nine contract sub-tables for a service
proposed: Read the contract of the sandbox build as the pipeline stage interface and its input and output profile: the stage contract document of 12.6, the seed profile schema as data, the database and role contract, the failure contract with the four legacy checks, the four fixtures and the nine tables. Publish it as a contract baseline in the repository beside the OpenAPI and AsyncAPI files so the same drift rule applies.

title: No source fixes the sandbox role name or the scope of the sandbox database for the 19-service target
source: Legacy RWB-E1-065 sections 3, 4 and 13 (role rwb_sandbox_read, database rwb_sandbox, database renamed from rwb_sandbox_next); Architecture v5 Text Extract v1 slides 8, 11 and 29 (one login rwb_source_data, 19 rwb_* schemas, no sandbox role); Ownership Map v1
section: 3 Preconditions; 7 Acceptance criteria; 10 Authority; 13 Solution plan
description: The legacy story names a read-only role rwb_sandbox_read and a database rwb_sandbox for the monolith, and Architecture v5 names one login per service and no sandbox role or database at all. Neither source says whether the sandbox of a service keeps its own read-only role or is read through the service login, and neither fixes which of the 19 services own a sandbox database and which share one.
evidence: Legacy section 3 'The Entra ID group RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE exists and maps to the sandbox read-only database role' and section 4 step 10 'grants SELECT on schema recovery to role rwb_sandbox_read'; Architecture v5 slide 29 with the 19 service schemas and one login each, no sandbox row; slide 11 'One login: rwb_source_data'
proposed: Read the target as one DEV sandbox database per service release, rwb_sandbox for rwb-source-data with the build database rwb_sandbox_next, and one read-only role rwb_sandbox_read holding SELECT on schema recovery and schema rwb_source_data and nothing on schema public, mapped to RWB-DEV-RW-TRIBE. The service login rwb_source_data keeps its own DML on its own schema. Confirm the role name in the Environment and Deployment Design before the first non-DEV use.
